title: Interim, negative: a trait-blind random dilution (p 0.05-0.20 per 10 frames) does not keep the Marangoni rods dividing; the chemostat returns matter at its own rate into the bath, so births stay at 0-5 per 20 frames and stop after frame 120 in all 8 settings (seed 80)
summary: Forked c34's Marangoni world with a dilution that removes whole bodies at random every 10 frames (raster-ordered bodies, RNG seeded only by seed and event index; world.py) and tuned it on seed 80 (150 frames): p 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, with kr 0.024, phi_b -0.58 and -0.56, and with the removed matter put back uniformly at once (REDIST). None reaches 12-20 bodies with >= 5 persistent splits per 20 frames; every setting has 0 splits in frames 120-150. At p 0.2 occupancy falls from 0.08 to 0.02 and mean phi stays below phi_b: births are capped by the chemostat's supply, not by space. REDIST at p 0.10 holds 21-27 bodies with up to 5 splits per 20 frames, the best setting; kr 0.024 forms nothing and phi_b -0.56 refills by nucleation. 0 of 54 dividing tracks swim 3 rod lengths. A T=2000 run of the best setting and its mar=0 floor follows.

finding.operator: trait-blind random whole-body dilution (serial-transfer turnover) on the Marangoni rods
finding.control: 8 settings on seed 80 against the no-dilution plateau of c00/c34 (occupancy ~0.08, ~2 generations)
finding.result: persistent splits after frame 60: 4-11 in 90 frames; splits in frames 120-150: 0 in 8/8; occupancy at t=750: 0.082 (p0.05), 0.024 (p0.2), 0.077 (p0.1 REDIST); D>=3: 0 of 54 dividing tracks
